title: Normalize Game of Life cells before toroidal stepping
description: Repo-global public-invariant audit found that step_game_of_life_cells wraps generated neighbor coordinates but checks survival against the caller's unnormalized HashSet. An L-shape crossing the left seam therefore loses live cells with two neighbors, and extreme i32 coordinates can overflow in x +/- 1 before wrapping. Normalize and deduplicate input cells once at the shared step owner, preserve byte-identical behavior for existing in-bounds animation seeds, and add one seam regression covering the public toroidal contract.
close_reason: Normalized and deduplicated the live-cell set once inside step_game_of_life_cells before neighbor generation and survival lookup. The merged boundary regression failed on a seam-crossing L shape before the fix and now proves seam survival, zero dimensions, and i32 extreme safety. Existing in-bounds animation behavior remains unchanged. Formatting, debug/release tests, strict Clippy, examples, CLI help, render_once, timed Game of Life PTY playback, Cargo package verification, Nix path build, and diff checks pass.

title: Keep Game of Life dimensions inside its coordinate type
description: Game of Life stores cells as i32 coordinates but repeatedly casts public usize dimensions with as i32. Built public-API probes prove build_live_game_of_life_seed(20, i32::MAX, bloom) panics multiplying a wrapped dimension and step_game_of_life_cells({i32::MIN}, usize::MAX, 5) panics in rem_euclid. Add one saturating usize-to-i32 grid-dimension owner, pass representable dimensions through all seed builders, preserve every practical-dimension seed and step result, and extend the existing boundary regression check.
close_reason: Game of Life now converts usize grid dimensions once into its representable i32 coordinate space, eliminating repeated unchecked casts across seed placement and stepping. Practical dimensions preserve their arithmetic exactly; huge dimensions saturate instead of panicking, with the two-thirds placement widened through i64. Verified the formerly panicking public probes, the consolidated boundary test, 42 debug/release tests, Clippy, examples, Cargo package, Nix, and Matrix PTY.

title: Reject empty Kitty sequences without clearing the terminal
description: A built public-API probe shows play_kitty_png_frame_sequence returns InvalidInput for an empty frame list but still emits 60 bytes of Kitty delete and clear-screen commands. Empty input is rejected before any image can be placed, so playback should return the same validation error without cleanup mutations. Reuse the existing draw validation owner and preserve all nonempty cleanup behavior.
close_reason: Empty Kitty frame sequences retain the existing InvalidInput kind/message and now return before image deletion or screen clearing. Public-API probe emits 0 stdout bytes (previously 60); all 42 debug/release tests, Clippy, examples, package verification, path-flake Nix build, and Matrix PTY smoke pass.

title: Browse native Anima styles with previous and next keys
description:
## Why

Nova screen popup already launches Anima as `yzs random`, but Anima treats every key as exit. Choosing another visual therefore requires closing and reopening the popup or invoking a specific style from the CLI. Previous and next keys would turn the popup into a lightweight visual browser without adding a menu or configuration surface.

## Contract

Consumer: standalone `yzs` users and the Nova full-screen Anima popup.

Trigger: while a native animation is running, press unmodified `Left`, `h`, or `p` for previous; press unmodified `Right`, `l`, or `n` for next.

Result:
- Switch immediately to the adjacent native animation in one canonical ordered list and wrap at both ends.
- Rebuild the selected producer at the current terminal size without leaving and re-entering the alternate screen.
- Preserve the original overall `--duration-seconds` deadline across every switch; navigation never extends a Nova welcome or popup time box.
- Keep resize handling and frame cadence correct for the newly selected style.
- Preserve existing any-key exit behavior for every non-navigation key.

The initial style remains the explicitly requested style or the style selected by `random`.

## Scope

In scope:
- Browse every in-process `AnimationStyle`, including Boids variants, Game of Life variants, friends and enemies, Mandelbrot, and Matrix.
- Give the ordered browse list one owner and use typed animation styles rather than reparsing display strings.
- Extend the existing terminal input owner to distinguish previous, next, exit, and timeout.
- Document navigation keys in `yzs --help`.
- Keep direct `yzs STYLE` usage and the Nova popup path working with the same behavior.

Out of scope:
- Do not add a selector menu, HUD, persistent overlay, animation-name toast, keybinding configuration, history persistence, or shuffle state.
- Do not include `static`, `logo`, `random`, or the separately executed `asciiquarium` as browse entries.
- Do not change Nova popup policy or Zellij keybindings.
- Add no dependency.

## Implementation Notes

`screen_runner.rs` owns the animation session and already has the required style construction, per-style cadence, resize, input, and duration mechanisms. Keep switching in that loop. Replace the boolean keypress result with the smallest typed action that lets non-animation callers retain their current exit-on-key behavior.

The ordered browse list must be the sole navigation source of truth. A style change should render its first frame immediately, then use that styles cadence. A `random` launch may choose its initial dogfooded style as today and then browse the full native list.

Nova currently executes the packaged Anima binary directly for the screen popup, so downstream work should only publish the child revision, update the Nova Anima pin, and verify the real popup. No duplicate navigation logic belongs in Nova.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Focused tests prove every accepted key mapping, non-navigation exit behavior, previous and next wraparound, and stable canonical order.
- A deterministic session test proves switching rebuilds the correct producer without resetting the original duration deadline.
- A PTY smoke run injects both directions during a time-boxed `yzs random` session and confirms clean exit and terminal restoration.
- Run `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo test`, `cargo check --examples`, `cargo run --bin yzs -- --help`, `cargo run --example render_once`, and `nix build .#yzs --no-link`.
- After publishing Anima and updating the Nova pin, verify the Nova screen popup can browse in both directions and still respects its configured duration.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if switching requires leaving the alternate screen or spawning one process per native style.
- Stop if navigation resets or extends the configured session duration.
- Stop before folding the external aquarium or card-like screens into the animation loop; that is a separate product decision.
- Stop if the design introduces a second style registry or a new dependency.

## Maintenance Notes

Dependency decision: crossterm already exposes the required key codes and modifiers. Expected package impact is a small Anima binary increase with no new store path or closure dependency.

title: Propagate current Anima renderer through Nova to Eonova
description:

title: Propagate CLI help output failures
description: Repo-global output audit reproduced target/debug/yzs --help >/dev/full panicking inside std::io::_print and exiting 101. run_screen_cli already returns Result, so the help branch must preserve its successful output bytes while returning stdout write/flush failures to the binary's normal error path. Replace panic-prone print macros in the shared help owner, compare output byte-for-byte, and verify /dev/full exits through the reported Result rather than a panic.
close_reason: CLI help now writes through locked stdout and propagates write/flush errors through run_screen_cli; the binary ignores secondary stderr failure and preserves exit 1. Successful help bytes match the baseline exactly. Verified 42 debug/release tests, Clippy, examples, Cargo package, Nix package/runtime, Matrix PTY, stdout /dev/full, and stdout+stderr /dev/full.

title: Emit terminal animation frames as synchronized updates
description:
## Contract

Consumer: every terminal receiving a full frame through `render_screen_frame`.

Trigger: static, logo, Boids, Matrix, Mandelbrot, or Game of Life rendering emits one complete screen frame.

Result: the ordinary clear, cursor moves, row clears, styles, and text are enclosed by exactly one `CSI ? 2026 h` / `CSI ? 2026 l` synchronized-output pair and flushed as one renderer-owned update. Unsupported terminals ignore the private mode and process the enclosed ANSI normally. Terminal I/O failure remains a bounded `io::Error`, and the end marker is still attempted after an enclosed write failure.

## Accepted implementation

`terminal_control::render_screen_frame` is the sole writer owner. It constructs the existing ordinary frame bytes, then uses the already installed crossterm 0.29.0 `SynchronizedUpdate::sync_update` implementation. Crossterm queues `BeginSynchronizedUpdate`, runs the enclosed write, executes `EndSynchronizedUpdate`, and flushes; the public renderer delegates directly to it. All styles continue through the same owner with no style branch, support detection, configuration, dependency, or public API addition.

The original 0.28.1 dependency note was stale after rebaseline; Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock resolve crossterm 0.29.0. Its exact registry source emits `ESC[?2026h` and `ESC[?2026l` and is MIT licensed. Ghostty documentation identifies unsynchronized large-screen redraws as a tearing source and directs applications to the synchronized-output protocol. The maintained contour-terminal protocol reference defines the same DEC mode 2026 begin/end semantics.

## Acceptance proof

One contract-first regression failed before the writer existed, then proved a multi-row frame larger than 8 KiB has exactly one begin prefix, exactly one end suffix, all content inside, and no newline-driven row wrapping. All 42 tests, strict all-target Clippy, rustfmt, examples, CLI help, `render_once`, git diff checks, and `nix build .#yzs --no-link` pass. A native Matrix PTY run completed cleanly with balanced synchronized-frame markers.

Direct EonTerm/Eonova acceptance and the Nova child pin remain downstream rollout work; no Eon, Orbit, Venus, Zellij, frame-rate, animation-content, or differential-rendering change belongs here.
close_reason: Fresh-eyes pass confirmed the synchronized writer and nested Result propagation are minimal and correct, including BrokenPipe propagation and end-marker cleanup. Renamed the regression after the renderer owner it actually exercises; all 42 tests, Clippy, examples, Nix, and native PTY checks pass.

title: Propagate stdout failures from rendering APIs
description: Repo-global output-boundary audit proved that render_screen_frame panics inside stdio when stdout closes even though its public contract is io::Result; the built-crate broken-pipe probe exits 101 at std::io::_print. cleanup_kitty_image and draw_kitty_png_frame use the same panic-prone print macros behind io::Result. Replace those macros with locked std::io::Write operations, preserve successful output bytes and eager Kitty cleanup, and verify the built public API returns BrokenPipe instead of panicking.
close_reason: Rendering APIs now write through locked stdout handles and propagate BrokenPipe instead of panicking; Kitty duration coverage is deterministic and no longer emits terminal escapes during tests. Verified 42 debug/release tests, Clippy, examples, package, Nix, Matrix PTY, and closed-stdout probe.

title: Re-audit and simplify Anima after the first repo-wide pass
description: Second repo-global fresh-eyes and isomorphic simplification run over the current Anima worktree after yzs-qg6. Review changed work first, then all source, examples, CLI, terminal lifecycle, packaging, tests, and docs. Fix only newly confirmed defects or proof-backed simplifications, preserve the active Matrix work and unrelated user changes, and verify the complete child command floor plus strict Clippy and targeted output checks.
close_reason: Completed the second repo-global pass. Fixed the public Kitty layout overflow with a regression assertion; made eager Kitty cleanup explicit; deleted unused Mandelbrot normalized-depth math and skipped interior-only scoring work; merged equivalent palette branches; narrowed private terminal styling to chars; simplified Matrix trail tone and the Nix package lookup. Verified 41 tests, strict all-target Clippy, examples, CLI help, byte-identical Mandelbrot snapshots, a timed Matrix PTY run, and the Nix path-flake build.

title: Make welcome accent coloring order-independent
description: Repo-global fresh-eyes pass found that screen_runner::colorize_body advances through the text in a fixed accent-list order. The narrow welcome copy places zellij before helix, so zellij is never accented, while wider copy works only accidentally. Select the next accent by its position in the remaining text, preserve existing ANSI output for already ordered copy, and add one regression assertion for both narrow accents.
close_reason: Changed the shared welcome body colorizer to select the earliest remaining accent instead of depending on accent-list order. The regression test first failed on narrow-screen zellij and now proves both zellij and helix are accented. Debug/release tests, strict Clippy, examples, CLI help, render_once, narrow timed PTY rendering, Cargo package verification, Nix path build, formatting, and diff checks pass.

title: Keep Kitty frame line positioning correct in raw mode
description: Kitty's graphics protocol defines C=1 as no cursor movement. draw_kitty_png_frame emits bare LF with writeln!, while Crossterm raw mode disables OPOST/newline processing; the built output probe for a 20-column frame captured 7 LFs and 0 CRs. After five columns of image padding, the centered attribution therefore begins five columns too far right. Emit explicit CRLF for terminal line movement, preserve all non-line-break bytes and error propagation, and verify the captured output plus package/runtime gates.
close_reason: Kitty frame line movement now emits explicit CRLF, so C=1 placements and centered attribution remain correctly positioned when Crossterm raw mode disables OPOST. The output probe changed from 7 LF/0 CR to 7 matched CRLF pairs, and deleting the CR bytes reproduces the prior stream exactly. Verified 42 debug/release tests, Clippy, examples, Cargo package, Nix build, Matrix PTY, and raw-PTY Kitty probe.

title: Build a mathematical animation collection for Yazelix Screen
description:
## Why

`yzs` already proves that native terminal animation can make the Yazelix welcome surface distinctive, but its built-in collection is concentrated in boids, Game of Life, and Mandelbrot variants. A coherent mathematical-art collection would add visibly different motion families while preserving the standalone plain-terminal contract.

## Evidence

- `../yazelix-screen/src/screen_runner.rs` lists the current styles and owns CLI dispatch.
- `../yazelix-screen/src/lib.rs` exposes a foreground-only `ScreenCell`; `terminal_control.rs` has background styling only as a private output helper.
- `../yazelix-screen/Cargo.toml` currently needs only `crossterm`.
- Main Yazelix consumes the published `yzs` package through `flake.nix` and the `yazelixScreen` revision in `flake.lock`.
- FrankenTUI documents compact equations for Plasma, Gray-Scott, Clifford attractors, and radial wave interference at https://github.com/Dicklesworthstone/frankentui.

## Scope

In scope:
- Deliver two enabling slices: reusable truecolor half-block field rendering and narrow scalar-density simulation helpers.
- Deliver native styles for multi-scale Turing patterns, primordial particle systems, Chladni cymatics, complex domain coloring, an attractor atlas, quasicrystal interference, Gray-Scott reaction-diffusion, Matrix rain, plasma, radial wave interference, Physarum trail networks, and later Lenia.
- Keep each effect independently selectable from `yzs`, bounded by the shared animation lifecycle, and usable outside Yazelix.
- Treat child publication and the main flake-pin update as an explicit integration boundary.

Out of scope:
- Do not migrate `yzs` to Ratatui, FrankenTUI, Kitty graphics, Sixel, or an image-backed renderer.
- Do not change main Yazelix welcome/session policy or make every new style part of the random pool without an explicit visual and performance decision.
- Do not combine all effects into one unreviewable implementation.
- Do not begin Lenia until the density-helper and Physarum slices provide real performance evidence.

## Implementation Notes

The half-block renderer blocks all dense field effects. Scalar-density helpers follow it and block Physarum and Lenia. Native Matrix rain is independent. Plasma and radial wave interference remain separate from quasicrystal plane waves. Land one effect at a time, reuse existing timing/input/resize ownership, and require a concrete dependency justification before adding crates.

## Verification

- Every completed child passes the standalone command floor in `../yazelix-screen/AGENTS.md`.
- Each exposed style renders nonblank deterministic test frames at small, normal, and resized dimensions without panics or stale cells.
- Each simulation has a representative frame-time or bounded-work check appropriate to its complexity.
- Published child revisions are pinned by main Yazelix before integrated runtime claims are closed.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop an effect if it requires host-terminal ownership, unbounded state, or a non-terminal graphics protocol.
- Split work further if a child cannot be reviewed and visually validated independently.
- Keep Lenia deferred if direct convolution cannot meet cadence after the shared helpers are proven.

## Maintenance Notes

Accepted after comparing formula-driven, fractal, artificial-life, and terminal-native candidates. Deferred alternatives include a general VFX framework migration, image-backed backgrounds, host-terminal shaders, and external aquarium/rain processes.

title: Generalize Yazelix Screen to render truecolor half-block fields
description:
## Why

Most proposed field effects need two independently colored vertical samples per terminal cell. The current `ScreenCell` stores one glyph and one foreground RGB color, forcing effect-specific packing and preventing a reusable truecolor field surface.

## Evidence

- `../yazelix-screen/src/lib.rs` defines `ScreenCell { glyph, color_x, color_y }` and the sparse `ScreenFrame` render closure.
- `../yazelix-screen/src/terminal_control.rs` already emits a foreground/background-styled glyph through a private helper.
- `../yazelix-screen/src/boids.rs` contains local half-block and background-tone logic that demonstrates both the visual value and the duplication risk.

## Scope

In scope:
- Extend the frame/cell contract so a cell can carry explicit foreground and background colors without effect-owned ANSI strings.
- Add a reusable dense field adapter that maps upper and lower RGB samples to `▀`, clips odd pixel heights, clears stale output, and reuses allocations across frames.
- Preserve ordinary single-color glyph rendering for existing styles.
- Define behavior for transparent/absent samples, zero-sized terminals, resizes, and color reset at row/frame boundaries.
- Add focused renderer tests and one small example or test fixture that makes visual inspection easy.

Out of scope:
- No Ratatui/FrankenTUI migration, image protocol, alpha compositing, sixel canvas, or general scene graph.
- Do not redesign every existing animation around the new adapter.
- Do not add a rendering crate unless measurement proves the current crossterm path insufficient.

## Implementation Notes

Keep terminal emission centralized in `terminal_control.rs`. Prefer a typed optional background on `ScreenCell` plus a field-to-frame adapter over preformatted escape sequences. Ensure Unicode width remains exactly one column.

## Verification

- Unit tests cover upper/lower color placement, missing halves, odd dimensions, clipping, resize shrinkage, and reset sequences.
- Existing styles remain byte/behavior compatible where practical and render without color leakage.
- Run `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo test`, `cargo check --examples`, `cargo run --example render_once`, and `nix build .#yzs --no-link` in the child.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if the API requires effects to construct raw ANSI.
- Stop and benchmark before adopting a broader rendering dependency.

## Maintenance Notes

This is a P1 enabling slice, not a user-facing style. Publish it before dependent effects; update the main pin only when a published consumer revision needs it.
notes: Accepted state: ScreenCell::truecolor requires a typed RGB foreground and accepts an optional RGB background; indexed cells retain their callback path. HalfBlockField stores reusable two-sample arrays, treats None as absent, clips out-of-bounds writes and odd heights, emits spaces for empty cells, and clears state on resize. ScreenFrame and HalfBlockField batch truecolor ANSI directly into row buffers through terminal_control::write_truecolor. Exact-width centered rows retain their owned buffers instead of cloning. Terminal color resets before frame and Kitty clears, after every printed row, on alternate-screen entry, and before alternate-screen exit, preventing inherited or partial-frame color leakage throughout the lifecycle. ANSI emission remains centralized in terminal_control.rs. Reusing the legacy single-color helper remains rejected because it changes transparent-background bytes. No rendering dependency or animation redesign was added. Verified with cargo fmt --all -- --check, cargo test (44 passed), cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings, cargo check --examples, yzs --help, render_once, and nix build .#yzs --no-link.
close_reason: Fresh-eyes pass completed terminal lifecycle resets and eliminated exact-width row cloning; full verification passes.

title: Add reusable scalar-density simulation helpers
description:
## Why

The half-block renderer converts finished samples into terminal cells, but particle trails and continuous cellular automata also need efficient scalar-field operations before color mapping. Implementing deposition, wrapped sampling, decay, and blur independently in Physarum and Lenia would duplicate the most error-prone numerical plumbing.

## Evidence

- The renderer foundation owns RGB sample emission, not simulation-field evolution.
- The Physarum particle model needs trail deposition, sensor sampling, diffusion, and decay.
- Lenia needs reusable wrapped scalar fields and bounded convolution over continuous cell values.
- Existing `../yazelix-screen/src/boids.rs` and `game_of_life.rs` each own specialized spatial state, with no general density-field helper.

## Scope

In scope:
- Add a small reusable contiguous scalar field with explicit width/height and allocation reuse.
- Support clear/fill, wrapped and clipped sampling, bounded additive deposition, decay, normalization, and one measured local blur/convolution path.
- Define resize behavior and prevent NaN/infinite values from entering palettes or terminal output.
- Provide adapters that let an effect map the scalar field through the half-block renderer without coupling simulation math to ANSI emission.

Out of scope:
- No generic tensor library, FFT framework, GPU path, arbitrary kernels API, scene graph, or replacement for effect-owned update equations.
- Do not force Gray-Scott or Turing patterns onto helpers that make their double-buffered update less clear.

## Implementation Notes

Keep the abstraction narrow and data-oriented. Prefer reusable scratch buffers and explicit boundary modes. Benchmark local blur before selecting a separable or summed-area implementation; do not add a numerical crate by default.

## Verification

- Tests cover indexing, wrapped/clipped edges, conservation for deposition before decay, blur symmetry, normalization, resize reset, finite-value defense, and buffer reuse.
- Benchmarks or timing tests establish a practical budget at representative 120x40 and 200x60 logical fields.
- Run the full standalone child command floor.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if the abstraction starts encoding Physarum or Lenia rules directly.
- Stop and keep an effect-local implementation if a supposedly generic operation has only one real consumer or worsens clarity/performance.

## Maintenance Notes

This is the explicit later-stage prerequisite requested for density-heavy effects. It depends on the half-block renderer; Physarum and Lenia depend on this task.

title: Add a plasma interference animation
description:
## Why

A classic plasma effect produces smooth psychedelic bands from a few moving sine fields. It is cheap, immediately animated, and visually distinct from cellular automata, particles, fractals, and radial wave interference.

## Evidence

- FrankenTUI documents its Plasma effect as the average of six animated sine phases in its VFX catalog: https://github.com/Dicklesworthstone/frankentui.
- The shared truecolor half-block renderer can preserve smooth gradients without full-cell vertical stretching.

## Scope

In scope:
- Combine a small curated set of spatial and radial sine terms over aspect-correct normalized coordinates.
- Animate phase and color cycling smoothly with bounded speed and no frame-wide flashes.
- Map the normalized field through a truecolor palette and add one `plasma` CLI style.
- Precompute frame-invariant coordinate terms and avoid per-cell allocation.

Out of scope:
- No shader runtime, arbitrary formula editor, audio reactivity, or direct FrankenTUI dependency.
- Do not merge this with radial `wave-interference`; they must retain different spatial structure.

## Implementation Notes

Expose the style through `ScreenStyle`, CLI parsing/help, and an explicit random-pool decision. Reuse the existing animation context for duration, input, resize, and terminal cleanup. Implement and verify in the child, push the child commit, then update only the `yazelixScreen` lock input in main Yazelix and verify the integrated `yzx screen` path.
Use FrankenTUI as a behavioral reference and implement the compact equation locally after checking provenance. Standard-library trigonometry should be sufficient.

## Verification

- Tests cover deterministic phase evolution, finite normalized samples, aspect correction, palette bounds, and resize regeneration.
- Visual fixtures confirm smooth bands, continuous color motion, and a nonblank frame at small, normal, and wide sizes.
- Run the full child command floor and inspect the real truecolor runtime.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if palette cycling causes flicker or abrupt global luminance changes.
- Stop if the result is visually interchangeable with quasicrystal or radial wave interference.

## Maintenance Notes

Dependency decision: blocked only by the half-block renderer. Add no VFX or math crate.

title: Add a radial wave-interference animation
description:
## Why

Multiple moving wave sources create expanding, colliding ripple fronts and moire-like nodes. This is a separate visual family from quasicrystal plane waves and plasma color bands, and it can react naturally to terminal geometry.

## Evidence

- FrankenTUI documents Wave Interference as `I(x,t) = sum sin(k_i * |x-s_i| - omega_i*t)` in its VFX catalog: https://github.com/Dicklesworthstone/frankentui.
- The existing quasicrystal bead uses oriented plane waves; radial distance to discrete sources yields materially different concentric collisions.

## Scope

In scope:
- Implement a bounded set of radial wave sources with curated frequency, phase, amplitude, and slow source motion.
- Correct distance for terminal aspect ratio and map signed interference to a stable truecolor palette.
- Keep source count and per-frame work bounded; precompute or reuse coordinate data where useful.
- Add one `wave-interference` CLI style.

Out of scope:
- No physical fluid solver, reflection/refraction model, interactive mouse sources, audio input, or arbitrary source editor.
- Do not collapse the bead into plasma or quasicrystal rendering.

## Implementation Notes

Expose the style through `ScreenStyle`, CLI parsing/help, and an explicit random-pool decision. Reuse the existing animation context for duration, input, resize, and terminal cleanup. Implement and verify in the child, push the child commit, then update only the `yazelixScreen` lock input in main Yazelix and verify the integrated `yzx screen` path.
Implement the equation locally from the documented model. Keep wave-source state typed and deterministic.

## Verification

- Tests cover source-distance symmetry, deterministic motion, finite amplitudes, aspect correction, resize handling, and palette bounds.
- Visual fixtures show recognizable circular fronts and changing interference nodes at narrow, normal, and wide sizes.
- Run the full child command floor.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if source motion produces discontinuities or global flashing.
- Stop if terminal aspect correction leaves circles visibly elliptical in the supported runtime.

## Maintenance Notes

Dependency decision: blocked by the half-block renderer. Standard-library math is sufficient.

title: Add a Physarum trail-network animation
description:
## Why

A Physarum-inspired sensor-and-trail model forms branching transport networks, veins, loops, and pulsing fronts. It offers a denser and more structural artificial-life effect than boids or primordial particle clusters.

## Evidence

- Jeff Jones describes emergent transport-network formation from simple chemotactic particles in https://uwe-repository.worktribe.com/output/980579/characteristics-of-pattern-formation-and-evolution-in-approximations-of-physarum-transport-networks.
- The scalar-density helper provides the required trail deposition, sensing, diffusion, and decay operations.

## Scope

In scope:
- Implement a bounded deterministic agent population that samples forward/left/right trail sensors, turns toward stronger density, moves, and deposits trail.
- Diffuse and decay the trail field using the shared density helpers, with wrapped boundaries and curated parameters that form visible networks promptly.
- Render trail intensity and fresh deposits through a restrained truecolor palette.
- Add one `physarum` CLI style.

Out of scope:
- Do not claim biological fidelity, add food-source pathfinding, interactive painting, GPU particles, or millions of agents.
- Do not duplicate the primordial particle interaction rule or turn this into a simulation framework.

## Implementation Notes

Expose the style through `ScreenStyle`, CLI parsing/help, and an explicit random-pool decision. Reuse the existing animation context for duration, input, resize, and terminal cleanup. Implement and verify in the child, push the child commit, then update only the `yazelixScreen` lock input in main Yazelix and verify the integrated `yzx screen` path.
Keep agent state structure-of-arrays or otherwise cache-friendly only if measurement warrants it. Reuse the established deterministic PRNG rather than adding a random crate.

## Verification

- Tests cover deterministic sensing/turning, wrapped movement, bounded deposition, trail decay/diffusion, finite state, resize reset, and agent-count limits.
- Extended fixed-seed runs form connected trails rather than uniform fog or static noise.
- Measure representative terminal sizes, run the full child command floor, and inspect the integrated runtime.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if useful networks require a particle count that misses the frame budget.
- Stop if the density field saturates uniformly; correct the sensor/deposit/decay balance before integration.

## Maintenance Notes

Dependency decision: blocked by the reusable scalar-density helpers, which already depend on the half-block renderer. Add no simulation crate.

title: Add a deferred Lenia continuous-life animation
description:
## Why

Lenia can produce smooth, mobile, organism-like structures unlike discrete Game of Life. It is visually compelling, but its continuous convolution and narrow viable parameter regions make it a later effect that should build on proven density helpers rather than forcing premature renderer abstractions.

## Evidence

- Bert Wang-Chak Chan defines Lenia as a continuous-space, continuous-time, continuous-state cellular automaton in https://arxiv.org/abs/1812.05433.
- The requested sequencing is explicit: implement Lenia only after the renderer and scalar-density helpers have proven efficient with earlier effects.

## Scope

In scope:
- Implement one documented Lenia rule family with a bounded radial kernel, continuous growth function, stable timestep, and a small set of known viable seeds/parameters.
- Use wrapped boundaries, reusable scalar fields, and the half-block renderer.
- Preserve recognizable localized structures through resize by deterministic restart rather than malformed resampling.
- Add one `lenia` CLI style only after the prerequisite helper contract is stable.

Out of scope:
- No Flow-Lenia, evolutionary search, interactive taxonomy browser, arbitrary kernels, multi-species system, FFT framework, GPU compute, or claims of biological organisms.
- Do not start by generalizing every simulation API in the repository.

## Implementation Notes

Expose the style through `ScreenStyle`, CLI parsing/help, and an explicit random-pool decision. Reuse the existing animation context for duration, input, resize, and terminal cleanup. Implement and verify in the child, push the child commit, then update only the `yazelixScreen` lock input in main Yazelix and verify the integrated `yzx screen` path.
Begin with direct bounded convolution and profile representative sizes. Consider separable, sparse radial, or FFT approaches only from measured evidence. Record exact rule parameters and seed provenance.

## Verification

- Tests cover deterministic convolution/growth, finite bounded state, wrapped edges, timestep stability, seed loading, resize restart, and long-run survival of at least one curated pattern.
- Performance evidence demonstrates that the selected kernel and field size meet animation cadence without unbounded degradation.
- Run the full child command floor and manually inspect the organism at multiple terminal sizes.

## Stop Conditions

- Do not begin while the scalar-density helper bead is incomplete or still changing materially.
- Stop if viable patterns require an FFT/GPU dependency before direct measured alternatives are exhausted.
- Stop if the chosen seed dies or explodes under the actual terminal timestep.

## Maintenance Notes

This is intentionally P3 and blocked by the scalar-density helper. Keep it later than Physarum so the shared deposition, blur, boundary, and palette paths have real runtime evidence first.

title: Add a dense friends-and-enemies particle dance
description:
## Why

The documented friends-and-enemies particle rule produces vortices, tendrils, rings, and collapsing swarms from a very small O(n) update: every particle follows one friend, avoids one enemy, contracts slightly toward center, and occasionally rewires. This gives Yazelix Screen a dense generative particle field that is visually distinct from the current low-count sprite boids and from true Primordial Particle Systems.

The accepted visual direction is lots of tiny dots or blocks. The result must read as a dense swarm containing hundreds to roughly a thousand particles at common terminal sizes, never as a handful of large sprites.

## Evidence

- https://x.com/IsaacKing314/status/2086721066106253347 shows the desired high-density visual behavior.
- https://community.wolfram.com/groups/-/m/t/122095 documents Simon Woods original 1,000-particle rule, update equation, parameters, and rewiring rationale.
- `src/boids.rs:98-176` owns the existing 8-32-particle sprite animation and demonstrates the shared frame-producer lifecycle, but its visual identity and O(n²) neighborhood rule are intentionally different.
- `src/game_of_life.rs:83-94` defines `ScreenAnimationContext` and `ScreenFrameProducer`.
- `src/screen_runner.rs:11-35` and `src/screen_runner.rs:341-392` own style registration, construction, context, and cadence.
- `src/lib.rs:43-88` owns the current cell/frame surface.
- `yzs-mathematical-animation-collection-dou.1` already owns reusable truecolor half-block field rendering.

## Scope

In scope:
- Add one native `friends_and_enemies` CLI style implementing the documented simultaneous update:
  `p = 0.995p + 0.02 f(friend - p) - 0.01 f(enemy - p)`, with `f(d) = d / (0.01 + |d|)`.
- Give every particle deterministic initial position, friend index, and enemy index; occasionally rewire one particle using the same deterministic random stream.
- Use double-buffered positions so a frame does not depend on iteration order.
- Scale particle count with available half-block sample area while preserving a deliberately crowded result: at least 500 particles at 80x24 and at least 1,000 particles at 120x40.
- Render many tiny dots or blocks through the shared dense half-block field surface. Accumulate collisions as density or intensity instead of silently dropping most overlapping particles.
- Preserve terminal aspect ratio, bounded memory, deterministic resize restart, duration handling, any-key exit, and alternate-screen cleanup through existing owners.
- Add the style to parsing and help. Keep it out of the random pool until short-session visual dogfooding explicitly accepts it.

Out of scope:
- Do not replace, rename, or reinterpret the separate Primordial Particle Systems bead.
- No large directional sprites, social-network UI, graph visualization, user-editable relationships, particle-count CLI option, general particle framework, external process, GPU path, image protocol, or new dependency.
- Do not change integrated Yazelix welcome/session policy in this child issue.

## Implementation Notes

1. Add one focused animation module owning positions, friend/enemy indices, deterministic random state, rewiring, and reusable next-position storage.
2. Reuse `ScreenFrameProducer` and the dense half-block renderer; do not emit effect-owned ANSI.
3. Start from the documented coefficients and one curated deterministic seed. Add no tuning configuration until the default proves insufficient.
4. Rasterize point density into the half-block sample buffer with reused allocations. Prefer one restrained palette; velocity or density coloring is optional only if it materially improves legibility.
5. Register `friends_and_enemies` through the existing CLI construction and timing paths.
6. Record source provenance in a short source comment without copying Mathematica implementation structure.

## Verification

- Focused tests prove deterministic initialization and stepping, valid friend/enemy indices, simultaneous order-independent updates, finite positions, deterministic rewiring, resize restart, and the required 500/1,000 particle floors.
- A representative rendered-frame test proves collisions contribute density and the animation produces many occupied dot/block samples rather than large sprites or a sparse handful.
- Inspect deterministic frames at startup and after approximately 3, 10, and 30 seconds at narrow, 80x24, and 120x40 sizes.
- Measure a 120x40 frame with at least 1,000 particles and record whether it meets the selected frame cadence before changing the density floor.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo test`, `cargo check --examples`, `cargo run --bin yzs -- --help`, `cargo run --bin yzs -- friends_and_enemies --duration-seconds 3`, `cargo run --example render_once`, and `nix build .#yzs --no-link` must exit 0.
- Publish the child revision before any later main Yazelix pin update.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if the shared half-block renderer is unavailable; do not bypass it with raw ANSI or effect-local foreground/background packing.
- Stop and measure before lowering the 500/1,000 particle floors or cadence.
- Stop if the result reads as another boids preset, requires large sprites, or loses the dense dots/blocks identity.
- Stop if faithful bounded behavior requires a new dependency or broader simulation framework.

## Maintenance Notes

Dependency decision: standard Rust math and the existing deterministic-random pattern are sufficient; add no crate. This is an O(n) directed-relation particle dance, not a local-neighborhood artificial-life claim. Review should prioritize density, short-session visual payoff, deterministic behavior, and clean terminal teardown.
notes: Accepted state pending commit/publish: friends_and_enemies is a deterministic O(n) half-block animation with 960 particles at 80x24 and a saturating 1,600-particle cap at 120x40 and extreme dimensions. One relations vector stores each particle friend/enemy pair; two initialization passes preserve the deterministic stream by drawing all friends before all enemies while removing one allocation and one length invariant. Particle count derives directly from half the terminal-cell area, and projection relies on bounds-checked float-to-index truncation. Rasterization clears its reused density and half-block buffers, then accumulates density and paints the final collision color in the same particle pass, avoiding a separate full sample-area scan. The private particle state remains finite by construction and bounded normalized updates, so projection does not repeat unreachable NaN/infinity guards for every particle; the 600-frame contract test retains the finite-state proof. The documented simultaneous coefficients are locked by an explicit stack-only equation/order test; the consolidated contract tests real 80x24 and resized 120x40 animation state, relation bounds, collisions, dense block output, long-run finite/dense state, deterministic rewiring, resize restart, and overflow capping. random.rs owns the shared size-derived seed and seeded-index mechanisms used by Boids, Matrix, and friends_and_enemies. Rewiring intentionally uses the terminal-cadence 75% gate but changes at most one particle per frame: testing the source roughly 10% gate collapsed this deterministic terminal seed to 42 occupied samples after 600 frames, below the accepted greater-than-150 density floor. The standalone play_style library example now parses, constructs, sizes, and paces friends_and_enemies, and its README command is documented; executing one bounded frame succeeds. The 80x24 ANSI capture remains byte-identical across core simplifications. cargo fmt, strict Clippy, 46 debug and release tests, examples, CLI help, render_once, a 3.014-second PTY run, and nix build pass. The module is 247 lines; the installed package remains 787,744 bytes with 8 closure paths and a 50,208,656-byte closure.
close_reason: Implemented and verified the dense deterministic friends-and-enemies animation, native CLI registration, collision-aware half-block rendering, standalone example support, and documentation. All 46 debug/release tests, strict Clippy, examples, timed PTY playback, and the Nix package pass; published artifact metrics are recorded in the accepted notes.

title: Add a multi-scale Turing pattern animation
description:
## Why

Multi-scale Turing patterns produce continuously reorganizing spots, stripes, membranes, and cellular forms from a compact local algorithm. They would be materially different from both Game of Life and Mandelbrot while fitting the existing finite grid model.

## Evidence

- Jonathan McCabe describes the multi-scale activator/inhibitor algorithm and least-variation scale selection in https://archive.bridgesmathart.org/2010/bridges2010-387.pdf.
- `../yazelix-screen/src/game_of_life.rs` already owns a resize-aware grid animation lifecycle that can inform, but should not be coupled to, this implementation.

## Scope

In scope:
- Implement a bounded scalar field with periodic boundaries, multiple activator/inhibitor radii, least-variation scale selection, normalization, and animated truecolor mapping.
- Choose a small curated parameter set that yields distinct stable motion at terminal sizes.
- Avoid per-cell heap allocation and reuse all scale buffers.
- Add one `turing` CLI style with deterministic seeded initialization.

Out of scope:
- No arbitrary user formula language, GPU compute, FFT dependency, or exact reproduction of every paper figure.
- Do not alias this to Gray-Scott; the update rule and visual identity must remain distinct.

## Implementation Notes

Expose the style through `ScreenStyle`, CLI parsing/help, and the appropriate random-pool decision. Reuse the existing animation context for duration, input, and resize handling. Implement and verify in the child, push the child commit, then update only the `yazelixScreen` lock input in main Yazelix and verify the integrated `yzx screen` path.
Start with separable box filters or summed-area methods only if profiling justifies them. Record the algorithm and boundary convention in a short source comment.

## Verification

- Tests prove deterministic updates, finite normalized values, periodic edges, resize reinitialization, and no blank frame for representative seeds.
- Measure a representative 120x40 run and keep frame work bounded enough for the existing cadence.
- Run the full child command floor and manually inspect at least small, normal, and wide terminals.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if the naive multi-radius implementation misses frame cadence; optimize the field passes before reducing correctness.
- Stop if the result is visually indistinguishable from Gray-Scott.

## Maintenance Notes

Dependency decision: blocked by the reusable half-block field renderer. Add no numerical crate unless a measured hot path and maintenance benefit justify it.

title: Add a primordial particle systems animation
description:
## Why

Primordial Particle Systems can form rotating clusters, membranes, and cell-like structures from simple self-propelled particle interactions. This adds an artificial-life family that is more organic and emergent than boids without requiring an external process.

## Evidence

- The University of Graz PPS project documents self-structuring, self-maintaining particle systems at https://alife.uni-graz.at/projects/primordial-particle-systems/.
- `../yazelix-screen/src/boids.rs` already demonstrates deterministic particles, wrapped bounds, spatial reasoning, and terminal color composition.

## Scope

In scope:
- Implement one documented PPS interaction rule with bounded particle count, deterministic seed, wrapped space, and stable timestep.
- Render density, trails, or local orientation through the shared field renderer so clusters remain legible without one glyph per particle.
- Curate parameters that reliably form visible structures within a short welcome-screen duration.
- Add one `primordial` CLI style.

Out of scope:
- Do not call the animation biological simulation, add reproduction claims not present in the implemented rule, or build an interactive parameter laboratory.
- Do not fork the boids module or duplicate its lifecycle and pseudo-random utilities wholesale.

## Implementation Notes

Expose the style through `ScreenStyle`, CLI parsing/help, and the appropriate random-pool decision. Reuse the existing animation context for duration, input, and resize handling. Implement and verify in the child, push the child commit, then update only the `yazelixScreen` lock input in main Yazelix and verify the integrated `yzx screen` path.
Extract a tiny shared deterministic PRNG or toroidal-distance helper only if it reduces real duplication. Keep simulation state owned by the new module.

## Verification

- Tests cover deterministic stepping, finite positions/headings, wrapping, resize behavior, and particle-count bounds.
- A fixed-seed visual fixture shows coherent clustering rather than uniform noise at 3, 10, and 30 seconds.
- Run the child command floor and inspect small, normal, and wide terminals.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if attractive structures require an unbounded warm-up or particle count.
- Stop if the rendered result reads as a second boids preset; revisit the interaction rule before integration.

## Maintenance Notes

Dependency decision: blocked by the half-block field renderer. Prefer existing in-repo math and PRNG patterns; add no simulation framework.

title: Add a Chladni cymatics animation
description:
## Why

Animated Chladni nodal patterns give `yzs` crisp, symmetric geometric motion that remains recognizable at low terminal resolution and contrasts with stochastic particle effects.

## Evidence

- Paul Bourke summarizes practical Chladni equations and mode combinations at https://www.paulbourke.net/geometry/chladni/.
- The proposed half-block field renderer can represent signed amplitude and emphasize nodal lines with truecolor shading.

## Scope

In scope:
- Evaluate a documented rectangular-plate Chladni field over normalized terminal coordinates.
- Animate mode numbers, phase, or contour threshold through a curated bounded sequence without abrupt blank transitions.
- Color nodal proximity and field sign so lines stay crisp on dark and light terminal backgrounds.
- Add one `chladni` CLI style.

Out of scope:
- No audio input, physical plate solver, arbitrary equation parser, or claim of acoustically exact material simulation.
- Do not render only a static contour.

## Implementation Notes

Expose the style through `ScreenStyle`, CLI parsing/help, and the appropriate random-pool decision. Reuse the existing animation context for duration, input, and resize handling. Implement and verify in the child, push the child commit, then update only the `yazelixScreen` lock input in main Yazelix and verify the integrated `yzx screen` path.
Keep trigonometric work predictable; precompute coordinate terms when they survive a frame. Handle aspect ratio explicitly because terminal cells are not square.

## Verification

- Tests cover symmetry for fixed modes, finite values, aspect correction, deterministic transitions, and resize regeneration.
- Visual checks confirm centered, nonblank nodal structures at narrow, normal, and wide dimensions.
- Run the full child command floor.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if mode interpolation collapses the field to a blank or saturated frame.
- Stop if aspect correction makes the output visibly stretched in common terminals.

## Maintenance Notes

Dependency decision: blocked by the half-block field renderer. Standard-library trigonometry is sufficient; add no math dependency.

title: Add a complex domain coloring animation
description:
## Why

Domain coloring turns complex phase and magnitude into continuous color, producing high-detail mathematical images with motion from very small formula changes. It would be the strongest color-focused style in the native collection.

## Evidence

- Wegert describes enhanced phase portraits and domain-coloring conventions in https://arxiv.org/abs/1007.2295.
- `../yazelix-screen/src/mandelbrot.rs` already establishes normalized complex-plane sampling and palette ownership in a native style.

## Scope

In scope:
- Implement a small typed registry of safe complex functions and animated parameters.
- Map argument to hue and magnitude to bounded lightness/chroma, with optional contour cues that remain legible at terminal resolution.
- Handle poles, zeros, overflow, and non-finite values explicitly rather than leaking invalid colors.
- Add one `domain-coloring` CLI style and select a restrained default function sequence.

Out of scope:
- No user-entered formula parser, symbolic algebra, arbitrary code evaluation, or exhaustive complex-function catalog.
- Do not duplicate the Mandelbrot implementation under a different palette.

## Implementation Notes

Expose the style through `ScreenStyle`, CLI parsing/help, and the appropriate random-pool decision. Reuse the existing animation context for duration, input, and resize handling. Implement and verify in the child, push the child commit, then update only the `yazelixScreen` lock input in main Yazelix and verify the integrated `yzx screen` path.
Introduce a tiny internal complex-number type if the existing code lacks one; a new crate needs explicit comparison against that bounded implementation. Keep color conversion in one tested helper.

## Verification

- Tests cover known phase values, zeros/poles, finite color channels, deterministic function transitions, and aspect-correct sampling.
- Visual fixtures show phase continuity and distinguish at least three curated functions.
- Run the full child command floor and inspect truecolor output in the real runtime.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if singularities panic or smear terminal state with invalid ANSI.
- Stop if the palette bands or flickers enough to obscure function structure.

## Maintenance Notes

Dependency decision: blocked by the half-block field renderer. Keep formulas source-documented and the registry intentionally small.

title: Add an attractor atlas animation
description:
## Why

A curated attractor atlas can produce luminous, evolving point clouds and trails while keeping the implementation compact. It directly adapts the visual direction of FrankenTUI VFX without adopting an entire UI framework.

## Evidence

- FrankenTUI publishes its terminal VFX implementation at https://github.com/Dicklesworthstone/frankentui and demonstrates an Attractor effect on https://frankentui.com/web.
- `../yazelix-screen/src/boids.rs` already renders accumulated spatial motion with terminal-safe colors.

## Scope

In scope:
- Implement a typed registry of a few documented attractors such as Clifford and Peter de Jong, each with curated stable parameters.
- Iterate a bounded point history into a decaying density field with truecolor mapping and deterministic style transitions.
- Reset safely on resize or divergent/non-finite state.
- Add one `attractors` CLI style.

Out of scope:
- Do not vendor FrankenTUI, copy code before checking its license and ownership, or create a generic VFX trait hierarchy.
- No interactive parameter browser or unbounded trail buffer.

## Implementation Notes

Expose the style through `ScreenStyle`, CLI parsing/help, and the appropriate random-pool decision. Reuse the existing animation context for duration, input, and resize handling. Implement and verify in the child, push the child commit, then update only the `yazelixScreen` lock input in main Yazelix and verify the integrated `yzx screen` path.
Use upstream as behavioral reference; implement formulas locally from primary documentation when that is simpler and clearer. Record formula sources and parameter ranges beside the registry.

## Verification

- Tests cover deterministic iteration, divergence recovery, bounded history/density, palette output, and resize reset.
- Fixed-seed visual fixtures distinguish each attractor and remain nonblank within the welcome duration.
- Run the full child command floor and inspect the published runtime.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if an attractor needs unbounded accumulation to become visible.
- Stop if upstream code provenance or license is unclear; use formula references instead of copying.

## Maintenance Notes

Dependency decision: blocked by the half-block field renderer. The atlas is one style with a small registry, not one CLI style per equation.

title: Add a quasicrystal interference animation
description:
## Why

Summed plane waves create ordered but non-periodic interference patterns with strong rotational symmetry. Slow phase and angle changes can produce a polished ambient animation with less simulation state than cellular effects.

## Evidence

- Wave-interference constructions for quasicrystalline patterns are discussed in https://arxiv.org/abs/2011.12383.
- The shared field renderer provides the density and color resolution needed to avoid coarse full-cell banding.

## Scope

In scope:
- Sum a curated odd-numbered set of plane waves over aspect-correct normalized coordinates.
- Animate phase, radial scale, or a bounded orientation parameter while preserving coherent symmetry.
- Map amplitude to a truecolor palette with no frame-wide flashing or clipping.
- Add one `quasicrystal` CLI style.

Out of scope:
- No crystallography simulator, 3D diffraction model, arbitrary wave editor, FFT, or shader runtime.
- Do not accept visually redundant presets that differ only by hue.

## Implementation Notes

Expose the style through `ScreenStyle`, CLI parsing/help, and the appropriate random-pool decision. Reuse the existing animation context for duration, input, and resize handling. Implement and verify in the child, push the child commit, then update only the `yazelixScreen` lock input in main Yazelix and verify the integrated `yzx screen` path.
Precompute direction vectors and coordinate factors that do not change each frame. Make terminal aspect correction explicit and keep wave count small enough for predictable CPU use.

## Verification

- Tests cover rotational symmetry within tolerance, finite amplitudes, deterministic phase stepping, resize behavior, and palette bounds.
- Visual fixtures show non-periodic structure and smooth motion at narrow, normal, and wide dimensions.
- Run the full child command floor.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if motion aliases into rapid flashing at normal frame cadence.
- Stop if the pattern becomes periodic stripes because too few or incorrectly oriented waves are used.

## Maintenance Notes

Dependency decision: blocked by the half-block field renderer. Standard-library trigonometry should be enough.

title: Add a Gray-Scott reaction-diffusion animation
description:
## Why

Gray-Scott reaction-diffusion produces moving spots, mitosis-like forms, waves, and coral textures. It adds a recognizable continuous cellular simulation whose behavior is distinct from the discrete Game of Life variants.

## Evidence

- Pearson maps Gray-Scott parameter regimes and patterns in https://arxiv.org/abs/patt-sol/9304003.
- `../yazelix-screen/src/game_of_life.rs` demonstrates grid lifecycle and resizing, while the new field renderer can display continuous concentrations.

## Scope

In scope:
- Implement double-buffered A/B concentration fields, a documented Laplacian stencil, bounded timestep, and periodic boundaries.
- Seed deterministic perturbations and curate a small sequence of feed/kill parameter regimes with visibly different behavior.
- Color concentration and gradient without hiding the morphology.
- Add one `gray-scott` CLI style.

Out of scope:
- No PDE framework, GPU compute, arbitrary parameter UI, scientific-accuracy claims, or shared state with Game of Life.
- Do not collapse this into the Turing-pattern implementation.

## Implementation Notes

Expose the style through `ScreenStyle`, CLI parsing/help, and the appropriate random-pool decision. Reuse the existing animation context for duration, input, and resize handling. Implement and verify in the child, push the child commit, then update only the `yazelixScreen` lock input in main Yazelix and verify the integrated `yzx screen` path.
Reuse buffers across frames and clamp or otherwise defend concentration bounds after each integration step. Document stencil, timestep, and boundary choices.

## Verification

- Tests cover deterministic seeds, finite bounded concentrations, mass/update invariants appropriate to the chosen discretization, periodic edges, and resize reset.
- Long-run tests catch numerical explosion; visual fixtures identify at least two parameter regimes.
- Run the full child command floor and manually inspect runtime cadence.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if the selected timestep becomes unstable over an extended run.
- Stop if all curated regimes converge to blank or uniform fields within normal display duration.

## Maintenance Notes

Dependency decision: blocked by the half-block field renderer. Add no numerical crate unless benchmarks demonstrate a concrete need.

title: Add a native Matrix rain animation
description:
## Why

Matrix rain is immediately legible, visually strong in a terminal, and can be implemented natively without the external Perl/runtime boundary used by asciiquarium. It also gives `yzs` a typography-driven effect rather than another mathematical field.

## Evidence

- Rusty Rain is a Rust terminal implementation and visual reference at https://github.com/cowboy8625/rusty-rain.
- The `matrix-rain` crate documents a reusable implementation at https://docs.rs/matrix-rain/latest/matrix_rain/, but adopting it is not automatically preferable to a small native module.
- `../yazelix-screen/src/screen_runner.rs` distinguishes native animations from the bounded external asciiquarium process.

## Scope

In scope:
- Implement bounded columns with randomized speed, head intensity, glyph mutation, and decaying trails.
- Use only one-column terminal-safe glyphs and deterministic local randomness.
- Clear correctly on resize and termination, and add one `matrix` CLI style.
- Compare local implementation with Rusty Rain and the `matrix-rain` crate for behavior, license, dependencies, and Nix impact before deciding whether to reuse code or a crate.

Out of scope:
- No external process, Perl dependency, font-specific wide glyphs, Katakana correctness claim, or full-screen TUI framework.
- Do not add configuration flags until one curated default proves useful.

## Implementation Notes

Expose the style through `ScreenStyle`, CLI parsing/help, and the appropriate random-pool decision. Reuse the existing animation context for duration, input, and resize handling. Implement and verify in the child, push the child commit, then update only the `yazelixScreen` lock input in main Yazelix and verify the integrated `yzx screen` path.
Keep the column model native to the existing frame producer. A dependency is acceptable only if it materially reduces owned code and preserves the lifecycle contract; otherwise implement the small state machine locally.

## Verification

- Tests cover deterministic column evolution, trail decay, one-column glyph widths, resize shrink/grow, and bounded memory.
- Visual checks confirm bright heads, readable trails, varied speeds, and no stale columns after exit.
- Run the full child command floor and verify `yzs matrix` and integrated `yzx screen matrix`.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if an upstream choice introduces its own terminal ownership or event loop.
- Stop if selected glyphs have ambiguous or double width in supported terminals.

## Maintenance Notes

Dependency decision: independent of the half-block renderer. Keep this bead ready so it can land while field-renderer work proceeds.
notes: Accepted child state: native Matrix rain with no new dependency or external process. It renders one bounded deterministic stream per terminal column with randomized speed and phase, changing single-column ASCII glyphs, white heads, fading green trails, a dense initial frame, deterministic respawn, wrapping frame arithmetic, and reset-on-resize behavior verified down to 1x1. The public matrix style, frame producer, native example, CLI help/resolution, and balanced random-family selection are wired through existing owners. The shared animation loop owns any-key exit, configured duration, and resize; existing screen guards own terminal cleanup. Rusty Rain and matrix-rain remain references rather than dependencies because neither reduces the local state machine enough to justify terminal lifecycle, dependency, licensing, and Nix cost. Current worktree proof: cargo fmt check; 39 cargo tests in debug plus focused release tests; cargo check examples; strict all-target Clippy; yzs help; render_once; Matrix PTY runs at 1x1 and 2x1 with clean restoration; nix build path flake. Plain git-flake nix build requires src/matrix.rs to be tracked because git sources omit untracked files. Remaining release boundary: publish the child revision, update the Nova yazelixScreen pin and welcome style catalog/docs, then verify installed fresh-session yzx screen matrix. Keep this bead active until that coupled work is complete.

title: Constrain the published crate to runtime sources
description: Repo-global fresh-eyes pass found that cargo package includes .beads issue data and repository-only CI, Nix, and agent files. Define the smallest Cargo-native package boundary that retains the crate, binary, examples, README, and license; verify the packaged source builds and the full standalone command floor remains green.
close_reason: Added a Cargo-native package allowlist. cargo package now excludes .beads and repository-only CI/Nix/agent files, retains all crate sources and examples including matrix.rs, and verifies the generated 172.9 KiB package. Full fmt/test/release-test/doc/clippy/examples/CLI/render/PTY/Nix checks pass.

title: Bound Kitty frame waits by the requested duration
description: Repo-global lifecycle audit found that play_kitty_png_frame_sequence always polls the full frame_delay and only exits after duration.max(frame_delay). The public duration therefore is not a time box: zero or sub-frame durations wait at least one full interval, and all deadlines can overshoot by nearly an interval. Preserve first-frame validation/rendering and eager cleanup, cap each wait by the remaining duration like the native animation owner, remove the forced minimum, and add one zero-duration regression that cannot touch terminal input.
close_reason: Capped each Kitty input wait by the remaining requested duration and removed the forced duration.max(frame_delay) minimum while preserving first-frame validation/rendering and eager cleanup. The regression failed before the fix by reaching terminal input for a zero-duration sequence and now returns immediately after drawing. Formatting, 42 debug/release tests, strict Clippy, examples, CLI help, render_once, Matrix PTY playback, Cargo package verification, Nix path build, and diff checks pass.

title: Simplify and harden the Anima repository
